rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest candidate: chunk 1 line 6, "One frontier skill already reached you as a plain prompt. The second-pass walk-down against your plan file, where Claude asked you one question at a time about unresolved branches, was patterned on Matt Pocock's `grill-me` skill" — this is chunk 1's own opening content, so there is no prior in-file slide to draw on, but the sentence fully unpacks itself in the same breath (what happened + what it was patterned on) rather than assuming outside memory — the same shape the compendium's own rule-2 passing example uses. Verified live this session that the referent is real and not invented: `grep -n "Phase 4: Walk down the unresolved branches" curriculum/exercises/push-back-on-the-plan.md` -> line 50, and that exercise belongs to M2 (`plan-mode-done-right.md:34`), one module before this M3 lecture — so the claim is a true cross-module callback, resolved by content rather than requiring the reader to already hold M2's file in mind. Second candidate: chunk 2 line 11 opens "Security practitioners. The two curated skills compress decades of judgement" before naming which two — resolved two sentences later, in the SAME bullet (STRIDE, then access-control) — cataphora inside one paragraph, not a deck-spanning forward reference. Confirmed via `git show 96fb2a89 -- curriculum/lectures/skills-from-the-frontier.md` that today's only commit touching this file edited a backing-block source-stamp footnote, not body lines 1-40 — the body is unchanged from the last audited pass. Harm rule 1 guards against (a reader stuck on a referent with no way to resolve it) is not present anywhere in the current body.

Only cross-file callback in the current body: chunk 1 line 6 (quoted above) — names the source (Pocock's `grill-me`, and by content the M2 walk-down) and unpacks its claim in the same sentence rather than pointing at a file by position ("the second module said"), matching the rule's own stated passing shape. No other file-level callback exists in the body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Lecture headings should be claims per rule 15, but three remain noun-phrase/ratio labels with no verb/assertion: chunk 1 line 3 "What a skill is" (definitional label), chunk 2 line 9 "Borrowed judgement, or your own" (two-way label), chunk 4 line 20 "Two curated, one authored" (ratio label). None fits the stated NOT-violation carve-outs verbatim (orientation headers, catalogue entries naming their subject, phase/section labels inside a walk), though "Borrowed judgement, or your own" and "Two curated, one authored" read close to "catalogue entries naming their subject." By contrast chunk 3 ("Your authored skill starts personal, then compounds"), chunk 5 ("Three trust artifacts the next engineer checks"), and chunk 6 ("The tool flags; you make the call") carry genuine subject+verb claims. Harm check, applying the template's own self-classifying principle for rules added after its blocking/non-blocking list was written: the failure mode here is register/mood, not comprehension — no reader is confused by "What a skill is"; the slide's mood is simply a beat flatter than a declared law would be. That is "this could be tighter", not "I cannot follow this." This also matches the compendium's own documented history for this exact rule ("a rule that only ever produces notes is a rule mis-scoped") and Antti's own carve-out cited inside rule 15 itself ("not every header owes a claim"). Filed as a TODO, not a blocking finding.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: If strict conformance is wanted: recast as claims, e.g. "A skill is judgement someone else already packaged" (ch1) / "Someone else's judgement, or yours" (ch2) / "Two proportions, and only one of them you can author" (ch4) — otherwise leave as labels; this rule's own documented history treats that as acceptable for a definitional/enumerating lecture slide.

Maintainer block (line 45, "Lean pass 2026-08-25, Antti-directed M3/M6 shorten") already names and cuts four instances of exactly this class from this file (a design-commentary sentence, a kicker, a padding lead, a duplicate bullet) — confirmed absent from the current body by direct read. Closest remaining candidate: chunk 4 line 25's trailing sentence, "The curated skills come from people who did the work; the one you author covers what only you do." Judged as earning its slot: it is the concrete definition of the chunk's newly-bolded principle ("Don't make general what you don't practice yourself"), not a bare restatement of chunk 2's split — cutting it would leave the bolded law undefined at its one appearance. Chunk 5's closer (line 31, "the next engineer... can see the reasoning and check it against the code") specifies the mechanism the header names rather than merely echoing it, and "Go." (chunk 6 close, line 39) asserts nothing to cut — it is a bare transition, not an aphorism kicker restating a header or point line.
